class="font-[600] py-[3px] text-[1.25em]" style="line-height:1.3" data-anchor="%22aiwebsitebuilder%22meansdifferentthings" data-slug="%22aiwebsitebuilder%22meansdifferentthings207"><span data-slate-node="text"><span class="" style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">&quot;AI Website Builder&quot; Means Different style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">A lot of disappointment comes from category confusion. In practice, there are three categories. True AI generators (that create structure and styling) include Squarespace Blueprint, Wix AI, Durable, and Hostinger AI. Pro tools with AI assistance (where the quality ceiling is high but you&#x27;re driving) include Framer and Webflow. And then there are commerce engines with AI content help, where Shopify is the clear leader, but it doesn&#x27;t generate your site. If you pick the wrong category, you&#x27;ll be disappointed even if the product is good.</span></span></span></div></div><div class="w-full mt-[1em] mb-[1px]"><h3 data-slate-node="element" class="font-[600] py-[3px] text-[1.25em]" style="line-height:1.3" data-anchor="ecommercereliabilitystillbeatsaimagic" data-slug="ecommercereliabilitystillbeatsaimagic209"><span data-slate-node="text"><span class="" style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">Ecommerce Reliability Still Beats AI Magic</span></span></span></h3></div><div class="w-full my-[1px]"><div data-slate-node="element" class="py-[3px]"><span data-slate-node="text"><span class="" style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">Here&#x27;s my boring conclusion: checkout reliability matters more than AI headlines. When I ran the same purchase scenario across platforms, Shopify was the most consistently &quot;nothing weird happens&quot; experience, especially once you move beyond one product and one shipping rule. Squarespace and Wix handled mainstream ecommerce well for small-to-mid catalogs.</span></span></span></div></div><div class="w-full mt-[1em] mb-[1px]"><h3 data-slate-node="element" class="font-[600] py-[3px] text-[1.25em]" style="line-height:1.3" data-anchor="platformlockinisreal" data-slug="platformlockinisreal211"><span data-slate-node="text"><span class="" style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">Platform Lock-In Is Real</span></span></span></h3></div><div class="w-full my-[1px]"><div data-slate-node="element" class="py-[3px]"><span data-slate-node="text"><span class="" style="white-space:break-spaces;word-break:break-word" data-slate-leaf="true"><span data-slate-string="true">I attempted exports and migration paths across platforms. What I learned: you can usually export product data in some form, but you usually can&#x27;t export the site you designed.
